title: Partition identity from typed columns in DuckDB and PostgreSQL
question: Can the present partition identity be produced by a straight-line expression over typed columns in DuckDB and in PostgreSQL, equal to Python canonical_identity and the installed recursive data.ddo_identity?
method: Build 60 synthetic annotation-shaped partitions (440 items) with integer, boolean, string, list and absent fields, including control characters and non-ASCII text. Compare the Python reference with a DuckDB aggregate over an Arrow table, a PostgreSQL aggregate over a typed temporary relation, and data.ddo_identity over the tagged body. The PostgreSQL leg uses pg_temp in corpus_structure_dev and rolls back.

results.name: DuckDB typed expression equals Python identity
PostgreSQL typed expression equals Python identity
results.note: Set SQL over a typed temporary relation.

results.name: Installed recursive identity equals Python identity
results.note: Development database holds a prior root.

conclusion: For integer, boolean, string, list and absent fields the existing identity is reproducible from typed columns in both engines without changing its definition. Absent fields need explicit presence handling; the first run failed until they had it. Decimals, floats, timestamps, sets, bags, optional-value tags and nested mappings are not covered.
